notes: kcal and protein (grams) per ONE catalog unit of each ingredient (the catalog’s "unit"; "basis" says exactly what one unit is). Generic foods use USDA FoodData Central SR Legacy reference values (fdc.nal.usda.gov; NDB numbers cited where known) converted to the catalog unit; branded/packaged items use typical package labels. Lean meats (chicken, 93/7 turkey, pork chops/loin) use raw values. Ground beef, ground pork, Italian sausage and bacon are counted AS EATEN per pound bought (USDA cooked value × cooking yield), because the recipes spoon off or drain the rendered fat. Oil, butter, mayo and dressings count in full at recipe amounts. Canned vegetables and beans are per can as eaten (drained where the recipe drains). v2.2: items the family buys by brand (93/7 beef, Rao’s, Artesano, Tillamook, whole milk, fast-food-style fries, etc.) use that product’s label; fully cooked/heat-and-serve products use package labels. Values are estimates for planning — a kind guide, not a lab number. 2026-11-15 (v3, docs/spec/18-recipe-box.md): "carbs", "fat" and "fiber" (grams per ONE catalog unit) were added for every id. They are ESTIMATES from the same sources as the calories (USDA FoodData Central SR Legacy reference values for generic foods, typical package labels for branded ones), rounded, and checked so that 4 × protein + 4 × (carbs − fiber) + 2 × fiber + 9 × fat lands within 15% of the listed calories; treat them as a guide. "veg" is vegetable servings per catalog unit, where one serving is 80 g of vegetables or beans (about ½ cup cooked, or a big handful raw). Potatoes, sweet potatoes and fries count as the starch, and fruit is not counted, so they have no "veg".
